properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 8/03/2026 to TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC in Sugar Grove Township, Warren county. 102.4(d) - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL REQUIREMENTS – Person conducting earth disturbance activity failed to obtain other necessary permits and authorizations from the Department or conservation district, related to the earth disturbance activity, before commencing the earth disturbance activity, including the well permit.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 8/03/2026
Violation Code: 102.4(d) - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL REQUIREMENTS – Person conducting earth disturbance activity failed to obtain other necessary permits and authorizations from the Department or conservation district, related to the earth disturbance activity, before commencing the earth disturbance activity, including the well permit.
Violation ID: 8284098
Permit API: 123-49194
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Sugar Grove Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/03/2026
Comments: This follow-up inspection was conducted to document a field review of the recent removal of grub material previously located between the proposed Akins #3 and Akins #4 well pads. William Cenk and Brian Bennett of Trinity Mineral Partners (TMP) were present for the duration of this inspection. Brian Ayers (WQSS) and I, Mathew Haemer (WQS), were present to represent the Department.During the 07/21/26 JPA pre-application meeting between TMP and the Department, Department Technical Services staff requested that the grub material placed south of the roadway between the Akins #3 and Akins #4 well pads be removed as soon as possible to potentially restore the hydrology near the road and well pad construction back to its original condition. It was observed that the grub material had impeded and redirected the flow of an Unnamed Tributary to Jackson Run and had begun to cause E and S problems alongside the roadway, well pad, and below the well pad for the proposed Akins #4 conventional well.At the time of this inspection, it appeared that all of the grub material had been removed as requested. However, TMP had also elected to redefine one of the stream channels below the well pad for Akins #3 and direct its flow through the disturbed area south of the roadway to Akins #4. The excavation work related to this stream channel continues to cause erosion and sedimentation to occur alongside the roadway and well pad for the proposed Akins #4. This is not the outcome Technical Services staff intended to result from the removal of the grub material. At the time of this inspection, the newly excavated stream channel is unprotected from erosion. There are three filter socks installed south of the Akins #4 well pad beyond the excavated stream channel directly in line with this channelized flow. Filter sock is not designed to be installed in channelized flow. All three filter socks are being undercut by the channelized flow. Evidence of erosion and sedimentation is still present before and after each filter sock. The area south and continuing west of Akins #4 that is now accepting the flow of this stream water is beginning to erode. A forested wetland is located west and down grade from the Akins #4 well pad. Bank erosion and saturated earth below the wetland indicate that the stream water overflows the wetland during storm events.The Department has yet to receive an updated E and S Plan that meets the expectations of the Technical Services staff. It is recommended that no further earth disturbance occurs without notification to and approval by the Department.The encroachment violations and violations relating to erosion and sediment control continue in the present condition of this construction and related excavation work.The violation for failure to post the well permit during construction has been closed.

Comments: This inspection was performed following the Department receiving a complaint of possible brine dumping in a ditch line near the Brawand 53 well location. This inspection was performed with WQSS Rich Sheriff. The well is equipped with an electric powered pumpjack, and appears to be producing. The stuffing box seems to have leaked at times, as there is a coating of oil on the wellhead and ground. The well is tagged and the access road and site are stable. There is a ditch line/UNT to Johnson Run that flows near the entrance to this site. The ditch flows to the southeast and into a small pond approximately 500 feet away, which has an outlet to continue down-gradient. A check with a handheld conductivity meter and probe shows elevated levels in this channel immediately around a culvert and at various spots flowing downstream. There is also evidence of tree and other vegetative death along the immediate banks of this UNT, indicating that brine was likely discharged into this channel. (See attached photos) The Operator may contact WQSS Rich Sheriff at 814-723-0973 to discuss this incident.

Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 974740
Permit API: 081-20637
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Cummings Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 11/07/2022
Comments: On November 7, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline completed an inspection to follow up with a reported spill of production fluid outside of containment at the EQT ARO LLC Larrys Creek Fish and Game Well Pad C. Rick Hall with EQT reported a spill had occurred on November 3, 2022 at 2000, that a water truck leaked about 10-20 gallons of production fluid while loading. Mr. Hall reported that a clean up crew was scheduled to remove the impacted soil. The area of excavation was about 30 ft. X 15 ft. and only about an inch of soil was scraped up to remove the impacted soil. The impacted soil was placed in a covered roll off dumpster onsite. The DEP screened the area of excavation with a soil conductivity meter and measured 10 uS/cm to 60 uS/cm. The DEP observed some rust and pitting on the production fluid tanks. A hole was also observed in the liner of the secondary containment for the production fluid tanks. The DEP recommends monitoring the production fluid tanks and repairing or replacing the tanks as necessary. The DEP also recommends repairing the hole in the liner of the secondary containment as soon as possible to avoid a inadvertent release. The spill of production fluid outside of containment to the well pad surface is a violation of the Clean Streams Law 402(b), Chapter 78a.56(a), and Solid Waste Management Act Section 301. These violations have been immediately corrected.

Violation ID: 960902

Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/06/2022
Comments: On July 6, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a site inspection at the Range Resources Ogontz 3H, 7-9H due to a reported spill of production fluid (CTS 365323). Range Resources Kirby Steck reported a spill of approximately 2 barrels of production fluid to the well pad surface and off the pad on July 6, 2022. A water tanker back latch was not completely sealed and when they were adding production fluid to the tank it started leaking and spilled onto the pad surface and over the pad slope to low spot off the southeast end of the pad. The area of impact off the pad was about 60 ft. by 10ft and about 6 inches in depth. On the well pad surface the impact was approximately 15 ft. by 15 ft and Range Resources had only scraped the top layer of stone to remove the impacted soil. The fill slope of the pad had a 4 foot wide area of impact from the top of the slope to the bottom of the slope which is approximately 10 ft. long. Later in the day on July 6, 2022, Mr. Steck left a message with DEP stating that after removing all the impacted soil that the volume of the spill of production fluid was closer to 3 barrels. The contaminated soil was being stored on separate containment from the plugging operations. Range Resources was waiting for covered dumpsters to arrive onsite. Moody is scheduled to be onsite on July 8, 2022 to collect confirmatory samples and begin the Act 2 process.The spill of production fluid outside of containment and onto the well pad surface and off the well pad is a violation of the Clean Streams Law 402(b), Chapter 78a.56(a), and the Solid Waste Management Act Section 301.

I scraped a small area of gravel to assess the depth of staining and it appeared to be about two inches deep where I scraped. Operator, the Department requests that you inspect this area and contact the Department with your findings. Please ensure that your response is in accordance with 78a66. SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/08/2021
Violation Code: SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.
Violation ID: 919913
Permit API: 039-24590
Unconventional: No
County: Crawford
Municipality: Hayfield Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/08/2021
Comments: Onsite for an incident response to a reported release from the operator. The release was reported at 2:05pm on Monday, 6/7/2021. The release to the ground occurred as a result of the 4 1/2" casing pressuring up during routine maintenance on the well with a service rig. The 2" tubing was blown down prior to the incident. The estimated volume of oil released to the ground is 30 gallons. Consisting of pooled oil and misted oil around the rig and wellhead and spreading out within the hay field approximately 65-80 feet from the well. Approximately 19 gallons of pooled oil was collected and placed into the production tank. The vegetation (hay) that was covered with the mist of oil was cut down and bagged up for disposal. The majority of the impacted area was scrapped up with an excavator and loaded into a triaxle truck for disposal. Clean fill onsite was being applied to the excavated area as part of the cleanup/reclamation. The cleanup operation will continue Violations cite.

Comments: On 07/20/2026, a routine inspection was conducted of the Buffalo Township 1H well. The Erosion and Sedimentation Control General Permit (ESCGP) was terminated on 01/11/2018.At the time of inspection, the following was observed:- The PCSM BMPs are installed in the locations shown on the approved PCSM plan.- Scouring was observed at the outlet of Cross-Culvert 4 (Photos 15-17). This appears to be resulting in accelerated erosion at the culvert outlet and displacement of riprap apron material approximately 20 feet downslope of the culvert outlet, which appears to be compromising the ability of the riprap apron to reduce stormwater velocity. (Photos 15-17)- The Act 9 sign was present at the site entrance (Photo 1). - ERP and PPC plan appear to contain the components required by 78a.55. - The well site was exhibiting greater than 70% vegetative coverage (Photos 14, 18, and 19).- Well 1H appeared to be drilled and equipped for production. The well tag is installed in a permanent and legible manner (Photos 24 and 25). - No obvious fluid leaks or staining that would suggest a leak were observed at or around the gas wells (Photo 23).- The production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment do not have any observable fluid leaks (photo 20). The GPU/Vertical Separator Units are equipped with interconnected secondary containment drip pans (photo 22). This form of GPU secondary containment was approved by the Department for use on 6/21/2022.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for failure to conduct long-term maintenance at the outlet of Cross-Culvert 4, which appears to be resulting in accelerated erosion and sedimentation.

A water truck was scheduled to remove water in cellar in order to grease the valves. - Starting at approx. 10:35 ending annuli pressures were checked using a digital Crystal gauge. Gas checks were performed by Creston Reps., using a Bascom Turner Gas Explorer meter (cal. 11/10/22). Creston Consultant collected gas samples off annuli, where present, and will send out for isotopic analysis. Unconventional: No

Comments: This inspection is being conducted as a follow up to inspection 2995415 in which violations where noted for accelerated erosion rills along the access road and exposed soil on and adjacent to the well site. Comments: Incident Inspection of Chesapeake's "SGL12 L South" Marcellus well site.Chesapeake finished hydraulically fracturing the 3 Marcellus wells here in October 2022.Tony Savitski (Chesapeake) called the DEP on Monday January 16, 2023 (yesterday) to report an estimated 20 gallon spill of produced liquid from a vac truck to the pad surface. Chesapeake removed the visually impacted pad material and staged it on liner containment on the north corner of the pad. That material returned a >4.00 mS/cm electrical conductivity (EC) reading. I spoke with Andy Steffe and Ryan Carmody (both Creston Environmental) on site. They are screening the excavated area near the production tank for EC with a Hanna Groline Soil Test soil probe. Background pad material gave 0.07-0.19 mS/cm readings. Creston is collecting solid samples from the excavated area, and from the waste material on the liner.Violations for the produced liquid spill are cited to the 015-23622 well permit.Mountain Energy is cleaning out the 9 wheelie trailers that the 3 Marcellus wells were flowing back into.Vegetation and rock stabilize soil of the site. I did not see accelerated erosion or sedimentation.Containment structures are intact. I did not observe any leaks or other deficiencies.Post Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) controls are in place and appear to be functioning as designed. Pooled water on the pad surface in 3 separate puddles has electrical conductivity of 0.16-0.74 mS/cm with an Oakton PCTS 5.Air temp 36FJLP

Comments: A follow-up inspection was conducted after multiple releases occurred on Pad B. The wells on Pad B are in flowback. Secondary containment is installed surrounding the well heads. According to Zac Subra with EQT, earlier in the day less than 5 gallons of fluid was sprayed on the pad surface and onto the secondary containment around the well heads from a valve attached to a sand separator next to one of the well heads. The area of the pad surface had already been scraped by Tobias Machinery during this inspection. Some sand from the produced fluid spray was observed on the secondary containment.The sump remains installed at the northeast end of the north stormwater channel. The EC of this fluid was 3.55 mS/cm. The fluid coming from the seeps had a red/orange rust color to it. Mr. Subra said that EQT believes that the color is likely due to iron content in the soil. The fluid in the north central portion of the north stormwater channel had an EC between 3.55 to 3.76 mS/cm.Mr. Subra said that final samples have been taken for the Act 2 remediation report but that the sample results were not yet available as of the time of this inspection. Multiple evaporators are also in operation on Pad B. The secondary containment for the evaporators appears to be in good condition. Nine GPUs are present within secondary containment. The GPUs appear to be in good condition.On Pad A, six wells are still in production. Six GPUs are present and appear to be in good condition. The access road and adjacent pipeline right-of-way appeared to be dry. No new sediment discharges were observed. Some of the stormwater culverts under the access road were partially filled with sediment. Mr. Subra said that Tobias would be cleaning out the culverts later that day.Violations remain outstanding for the reported produced fluid release from the MASS on Pad B from 12/19/22 against permit 081-21881.Violations remain outstanding against permit 081-21879 for the reported release of produced fluid from clam shell boxes in the northwest area of Pad B, in the area of the dancefloor, from 2/6/23.Violations remain outstanding against permit 081-21880 for the reported discovery of additional fluid with elevated electrical conductivity in the northcentral area of the pad in the area of the Sand X boxes.

Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8240733
Permit API: 007-20640
Unconventional: Yes
County: Beaver
Municipality: Independence Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/07/2025
Comments: On July 8 2025, the Department conducted an inspection of the McMichael Well Pad in regards to a spill that was reported to the Department on July 8 2025 at 9:12am . Present during the inspection was Brandon Carson.The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspection, the Act 9 sign was posted at the access road entrance in accordance with 78a55. The Emergency Response Plan (ERP), and the Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency Plan (PPC), both of which contained all required components, were located within the on-site mailbox. The access road appeared to be stabilized with gravel.Upon arrival at the well site remediation efforts appeared to be nearing completion as the remaining excavated material was being placed into the roll off dumpster. Mr. Carson identified the location of the spill. According to Mr. Carson, ,the spill (which occurred on 7/8/2025 at 7:15am) was reportedly caused by a 2" hydraulic line failing on the snubbing unit during work on the 14H well. This resulted in a release of hydraulic fluid to secondary containment as well as the graveled well pad. Mr. Carson estimated 50 gallons of hydraulic fluid was released in total with roughly 35 gallons releasing to secondary containment and roughly 15 gallons releasing to the graveled well pad. A vacuum truck was utilized to recover standing hydraulic oil. At the time of the inspection, Specialized Professional Services Inc. (SPSI) was onsite remediating the impacted area.Mr. Carson stated the contaminated gravel was excavated near the initial location of the spill approximately 6-8 inches in depth. Additional gravel was excavated in the area the hydraulic fluid flowed to at a depth of approximately 1 inch. The excavated material was placed into one roll-off box located on site. The Department was unable to obtain conductivity readings in the location of the spill as the gravel pad was too heavily compacted. However, the spill appeared to be visually remediated in accordance with the current regulations.Upon inspection of the rest of the pad, the Department observed 7 other well heads which appeared to be properly tagged and surrounded by protective barriers. The production tanks and GPUs onsite appeared to be within secondary containment with no visible fluid leaks or spills.Based on observations from this inspection and information provided by the operator, it appears that the spill has been remediated in accordance with current regulations. Violations are being issued as immediately corrected for the release of hydraulic fluid outside of secondary containment.

Comments: On 3/22/23 an incident inspection of the Mac Well Pad site was conducted in response to a report of a spill that was reported to the Department on 3/21/23. Background:On 3/21/23 I received a call from DJ Hardy of EQT. He informed me that he had reported a spill to the Department's telephone hotline. The spill had occurred on the Mac Well pad when flowback was being conducted. EQT was investigating the cause of the spill but it appeared that the flowback had resulted in sand settling in the first tank in the series. The sand had caused the level of fluid in the first tank to fill faster than the subsequent tanks. The level rose and was released out of a valve at the top of the tank. The produced fluid misted out of the valve into the secondary containment, onto the gravel pad, and onto the northwestern vegetated slope of the well pad. SPSI had been contracted for remediation. Mr. Hardy stated he estimated that approximately 20 gallons of brine were released. I scheduled a field meeting with Mr. Hardy for the next day (3/22/23).During the inspection the following was observed:-An Act 9 sign was present at the site entrance (Photo #1).-Some residual sand was observed on the side of the tank that had overflowed, and some impacted fluid was observed in the secondary containment (Photos #1-4).-The secondary containment appeared to be structurally sound, and no evidence of leaks were detected (Photos #5-8).-Substrate appeared to have been excavated from the spill area and fresh gravel was observed (Photos #8-10).-Vegetation had been removed from the northwestern pad slope (Photos #11-12). According to Mr. Hardy, the production fluid misted the vegetation but did not appear to saturated the soil below the vegetation.-Two roll-off containers were present on the pad (Photo #13). Mr. Hardy stated that only one container was needed for the waste.-No elevated conductivity was observed in the spill area, immediately outside of the spill area, on the pad berm, or on the vegetated pad slope (Photos #15-18).According to Mr. Hardy, the spill outside of the containment has been remediated. EQT plans to clean the tanks, flush, and vacuum out the secondary containment to dispose of any impacted fluid.Violations of 78a57(a), SWMA 301, and 78a54 are being noted as immediately corrected.

Violation Date: 2/01/2021
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 914357
Permit API: 081-21803
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Lycoming Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 4/19/2021
Comments: On April 19, 2021, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted an investigation of a reported spill (CTS No. 356072) at the Beech Resources Premier Well Pad. Don Stevenson of Beech Resources reported on April 19, 2021, after removing the second AST off the well pad an area of high conductivity and staining was observed in the highly compacted soil where the tank was located. The estimated volume of the spill was about 500 gallons of production fluid. The area of impact was about 120 ft. X 150 ft. circle with varying levels of conductivity. A contractor was onsite beginning to excavate the impacted soils. The contractor was removing about 6 to 8 inches of impacted soil. The area of impact was screened by Beech Resources for conductivity. Areas where the compacted soil had already been removed had a conductivity near 320 uS/cm to 910 uS/cm. Conductivity of areas that had not yet been excavated at the time were around 1.69 mS/cm. There were no seeps off the well pad observed. Penn E&R is scheduled to collect confirmatory samples on April 20, 2021. This spill causes violations of the Clean Streams Law Section 402(b), Chapter 78a.56(a), and the Solid Waste Management Act Section 301. Outstanding violations from Inspection Reports 3139277 and 3141035 still remain.
